title: Generating Images and Video · Level 3
slo: Describe how diffusion generates an image from a written prompt.

exercises.question_text: What is repeatedly removed as a diffusion image develops?

options.rationale: Diffusion repeatedly removes noise. Structure emerges as noise decreases.
Bounding boxes locate detected objects. They are not removed during diffusion.
options.better_fit: Use them when reporting detected-object locations.

options.rationale: Class labels identify predicted categories. They are not the material removed in diffusion.
options.better_fit: Use them to represent classification results.

options.rationale: Filter kernels are used in convolution operations. Diffusion iterations remove noise instead.
options.better_fit: Use filter kernels for image-processing operations.

exercises.question_text: Which are parts of diffusion? Select all that apply.

options.text: It begins with random pixel noise.
options.rationale: Diffusion begins with random pixel noise. That is its starting visual state.
Prompt-related visual features guide what the image becomes. They connect the request to the result.
Bounding boxes are object-detection output. Diffusion generates visual content.

options.text: It assigns one category label to an image.
options.rationale: Category labeling is image classification. It is not part of diffusion generation.

exercises.question_text: Video generation can ignore the order of events over time as long as each frame looks realistic.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The clip could become logically incoherent.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Video generation requires temporal progression as well as realistic-looking frames.

exercises.question_text: For a dog-and-stick prompt, intermediate diffusion results progressively form the requested scene from noise.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The gradual formation of the scene would be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion produces increasingly structured intermediate results from noise.

exercises.question_text: What technique transforms random pixel noise into an image that matches a prompt?

options.rationale: Diffusion transforms random pixel noise into a prompt-matching image. It works iteratively.
Convolutional filtering applies kernels to an image. It does not generate a scene from noise.
options.better_fit: Use it to blur, sharpen, or highlight edges.

options.rationale: Object detection identifies objects in an existing image. It does not synthesize a prompt-matching image.
options.better_fit: Use it to locate objects in an image.

options.rationale: Image classification predicts a label for an image. It does not transform noise into a scene.
options.better_fit: Use it to assign a category to an image.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe image synthesis? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Image synthesis generates visual content. The content is requested through a description.

options.text: It can generate an image or video.
options.rationale: Image synthesis can generate images or video. Both are generated visual content.
Labeling existing images is classification. Synthesis creates new content instead.
options.better_fit: Use classification when assigning labels to existing images.

options.text: It finds object locations with bounding boxes.
options.rationale: Bounding boxes are object-detection output. They do not create requested visual content.
options.better_fit: Use object detection to locate objects in an image.

exercises.question_text: After each diffusion iteration, the model evaluates the developing image against the ___.

parts.text: After each diffusion iteration, the model evaluates the developing image against the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The developing image would not be checked against the requested scene.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The prompt, rather than a class label or epoch, guides the developing image.

exercises.explanation: The prompt guides evaluation of the developing image.

exercises.question_text: Which is a prompt for image generation?

options.text: A dog carrying a stick in its mouth
options.rationale: This is a natural-language description of desired visual content. It can guide a generated scene.
A bounding box records an object's location. It is not a requested scene description.

options.text: A list of pixel class labels
options.rationale: Pixel class labels describe segmentation results. They do not specify a scene to generate.
options.better_fit: Use them to represent semantic segmentation output.

options.rationale: A category is a label predicted for an image. It is not a natural-language request for an image.
options.better_fit: Use it as an image-classification result.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The statement is out of order.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the capability, the relationship it uses, then the result.

exercises.correct_answer: Image synthesis uses learned relationships between language and visual features to create images.
exercises.explanation: Image synthesis links language and visual features to create images.

exercises.question_text: In video generation, ___ means events unfold in a logical sequence over time.

parts.text: means events unfold in a logical sequence over time.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The temporal requirement would be misidentified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Temporal progression refers to logical event order over time.

exercises.explanation: Temporal progression names logical event order over time.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition does not read correctly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Define the prompt before stating what it guides.

exercises.correct_answer: A prompt is a natural-language description that guides desired visual features.
exercises.explanation: A prompt is a natural-language description that guides visual features.

exercises.question_text: The stages that progressively turn noise into the dog-and-stick scene are diffusion ___.

parts.text: The stages that progressively turn noise into the dog-and-stick scene are diffusion

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The process stages would be misidentified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion iterations are the repeated stages that progressively form the requested scene.

exercises.explanation: The dog-and-stick scene develops through a sequence of diffusion iterations.
